messages.text: Will a power spike fry the whole miner?

Great question — this is actually one of the Rev 6.1's standout design choices.

**The onboard F1 fuse takes the hit, not the miner.**

There's a small automotive-style blade fuse (the "yellow fuse") mounted **right on the board**, next to the XT30 power input. If a spike comes through:

- The F1 fuse blows first — it's the sacrificial part by design
- The electronics behind it are protected
- You replace a $0.50 fuse, not a $249 miner

Cheaper home miners often skip this entirely — a spike goes straight into the board and can cook the whole thing (or take the power supply with it).

**One more layer:** the included 350 W MEANWELL PSU is also a quality industrial supply, not a cheap brick — it's running at only ~30% load feeding a ~100 W miner, so it's not working hard enough to misbehave.

Not a "nothing can ever go wrong" guarantee, but the protection architecture is genuinely better than most at this price.
Is the included power supply actually reliable?

Yes — and there's a real reason, not just marketing.

**The M. LRS-350-12 is an industrial-grade supply**, UL/CE/UKCA certified, rated 350 W / 29 A. The NerdQaxe++ only draws ~100 W at full speed — so it's **loafing at roughly 30% of its cap····** 24/7.

Why that matters:
- Supplies run coolest and longest well below their rated load
- A cheap 99–124 W brick feeding a ~100 W miner is already near its ceiling — hot, stressed, more likely to fail and potentially take the miner with it
- This one has enormous headroom; it's barely working

**Bonus:** that same headroom means if you ever want to overclock via the open firmware, the PSU is already proven to support it — no extra parts needed.

It's also the same supply model used in serious overclock research on this chip, so it's not just "adequate," it's genuinely cap····hardware included from day one.
